evidence.title: Hacking PubChem: Query by SMILES
evidence.author: Apodaca, Richard
excerpts: Recently, I showed how a simple PubChem API could be built from a few lines of Ruby code.
The API we created could retrieve a molfile and a 2-D molecular rendering given a PubChem compound ID (CID).
In this tutorial, we'll see how a SMILES query mechanism can be added to the API, enabling CIDs to be retrieved from any valid SMILES string.

evidence.title: Positional Regularities in Canonical SMILES: Implications for Molecular Machine Learning
evidence.publisher: Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Department of Artificial Intelligence and Systems Engineering
evidence.author: Marosi, Márk; Antal, Péter
excerpts: These findings suggest that models trained exclusively on canonical SMILES may learn positional shortcuts rather than genuine chemical representations, with implications for generalization and robustness.
We propose random SMILES augmentation and representation-invariant evaluation as standard practice for molecular ML.
